items.heading: Mht
items.text: MHT-CET is the Maharashtra Health and Technical Common Entrance Test, run every year by the State Common Entrance Test Cell, a body under the Government of Maharashtra.

items.heading: This Is the Part Most
items.text: This is the part most generic "PCB career options" advice skips entirely.

items.heading: Bsc Nursing
items.text: BSc Nursing. Runs on a separate state exam, the MH BSc Nursing CET, not MHT-CET. Do not assume your MHT-CET PCB score works here.

items.heading: D
items.text: D.Pharm (Diploma in Pharmacy). No entrance exam at all in Maharashtra. Admission is purely on 12th (HSC) marks through the state CAP for diploma pharmacy.

items.heading: Bams, Bhms, Bums (Ayush Courses)
items.text: BAMS, BHMS, BUMS (AYUSH courses). These sit under the AYUSH admission process, which in most states currently runs on NEET scores, not MHT-CET.

items.heading: Mbbs and Bds
items.text: MBBS and BDS. Still NEET-only across India. MHT-CET has no role in medical or dental admission at any stage.

items.heading: IT Is Not a National
items.text: It is not a national exam. It is a Maharashtra state exam, run by a state body, mainly serving Maharashtra colleges.

items.heading: IT Is Not the Same
items.text: It is not the same exam as NEET, even though both PCB students sit a biology-heavy paper.

items.heading: IT Is Not One Single
items.text: It is not one single exam covering every health and science course, nursing runs on its own separate CET.
